## 20.8 AI Engineering Perspective

### An AI API playground

For AI products, a playground converts far better than reference docs, because the value is in the *output* and prose cannot convey it.

```python
@app.get("/playground", include_in_schema=False, response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def playground(user: Annotated[User, Depends(current_user_optional)]):
    """A minimal chat console with streaming, so a prospective user sees the
    product working before writing a line of code."""
    return templates.TemplateResponse("playground.html", {
        "models": await model_registry.list_public(),
        "default_model": settings.DEFAULT_MODEL,
        "demo_token": await issue_demo_token() if user is None else None,
        "example_prompts": [
            "Summarise the key risks in the attached document",
            "What was Q3 revenue and how did it compare to Q2?",
            "Draft an email to the customer about the delay",
        ],
    })
```

**Give anonymous visitors a rate-limited demo token.** Requiring signup before anyone can see the product work is the highest-friction choice available, and it is what most teams do by default.

### Documenting streaming for humans

```python
@router.post(
    "/chat/completions",
    summary="Create a chat completion",
    description="""
Generates a model response for the given conversation.

### Streaming

Set `"stream": true` to receive Server-Sent Events. Each event is
`data: <json>\\n\\n`; the stream ends with `data: [DONE]`.

> **Note:** the "Try it out" button below buffers the entire stream, so
> streaming responses appear all at once. Use `curl -N` to see real
> incremental delivery:

```bash
curl -N -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/chat/completions \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count to five"}],"stream":true}'
```

### Event types

| `type`     | Meaning                                    |
|------------|--------------------------------------------|
| `start`    | Stream established; carries the request ID |
| `status`   | Pipeline stage (embedding, searching…)     |
| `citation` | A source passage used for the answer       |
| `delta`    | A content token                            |
| `usage`    | Token counts and estimated cost            |
| `error`    | In-band error; the HTTP status is already 200 |
| `done`     | Completion, with `finish_reason` and usage |

### Errors during streaming

Because the HTTP status is sent before generation begins, failures arrive
**in-band** as an `error` event. Always handle it — a client that only
checks the status code will treat a failed generation as a short answer.
""",
)
async def chat_completions(...): ...
```

**That "Note" about Try-it-out saves support tickets.** Developers reasonably assume a broken server when Swagger UI shows nothing for twenty seconds. Telling them why, and giving them the working command, converts a bug report into a successful integration.

### Cost transparency

```python
@app.get("/v1/models", tags=["meta"], response_model=ModelList)
async def list_models() -> ModelList:
    """Available models with pricing, context windows, and capabilities.
    Poll this rather than hard-coding model names — we add and retire models."""
    return ModelList(data=[
        ModelInfo(id="gpt-4o-mini", provider="openai",
                  context_window=128_000, max_output_tokens=16_384,
                  input_cost_per_1m_tokens=0.15, output_cost_per_1m_tokens=0.60,
                  supports_streaming=True, supports_tools=True, supports_vision=True,
                  recommended_for=["general chat", "summarisation", "extraction"]),
        ModelInfo(id="claude-sonnet-5", provider="anthropic",
                  context_window=200_000, max_output_tokens=64_000,
                  input_cost_per_1m_tokens=3.00, output_cost_per_1m_tokens=15.00,
                  supports_streaming=True, supports_tools=True, supports_vision=True,
                  recommended_for=["complex reasoning", "long documents", "code"]),
    ])
```

Returning `usage` on every response, and cost per model here, lets developers build their own cost controls. Hiding it makes your API feel risky to adopt — which it is, if a bug can cost four figures overnight.

### Migration guides from other providers

```markdown
## Migrating from OpenAI

Our chat endpoint is OpenAI-compatible. Change one line:

```diff
- client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"])
+ client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["PLATFORM_API_KEY"],
+                 base_url="https://api.example.com/v1")
```

### What is identical
`messages`, `model`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`, `stream`, `tools`,
`tool_choice`, `response_format`, and the full response shape including
`usage` and `finish_reason`.

### What differs
| Behaviour | OpenAI | Us |
|---|---|---|
| Rate limit errors | `429`, `Retry-After` | same |
| Quota exhaustion | `429` | **`402`** with `code: quota_exceeded` |
| Unknown model | `404` | `404` with the list of valid models in `details` |
| Streaming usage | requires `stream_options` | always included in the final event |

### What we add
`GET /v1/knowledge-bases/{id}/queries` for RAG over your own documents —
see the [RAG guide](https://docs.example.com/rag).
```

**A migration guide is the single highest-converting page for a compatible API.** It answers the only question a prospective user has: how much work is this?

## 20.9 Backend Engineering Perspective

**The docs-as-code workflow:**

```
   app code (type hints, decorators, docstrings)
        │
        ├──► openapi.json  (generated, committed, linted, diffed — Ch. 19)
        │        │
        │        ├──► Swagger UI / ReDoc / Scalar   (reference)
        │        ├──► generated SDKs                (with docstrings)
        │        └──► x-codeSamples                 (curl/Python/TS)
        │
   docs/ (Markdown, in the same repo)
        │
        └──► static site (Mintlify / Docusaurus / Starlight)
                 │
                 └──► docs.example.com  — reference + guides together
```

**Keep the guides in the same repository as the code.** A guide in a separate CMS drifts within one sprint; a guide in `docs/` next to the code it describes gets updated in the same pull request, and can be tested.

**Test your documentation examples.** This is unusual and disproportionately valuable:

```python
# tests/docs/test_examples.py
import re, pathlib

def extract_python_blocks(markdown: str) -> list[str]:
    return re.findall(r"```python\n(.*?)```", markdown, re.DOTALL)

@pytest.mark.parametrize("doc_path", list(pathlib.Path("docs").rglob("*.md")),
                         ids=lambda p: str(p))
def test_documentation_examples_are_valid(doc_path, live_server, api_key):
    for i, block in enumerate(extract_python_blocks(doc_path.read_text())):
        if "# doctest: skip" in block:
            continue
        namespace = {"BASE_URL": live_server, "API_KEY": api_key}
        try:
            exec(compile(block, f"{doc_path}:block{i}", "exec"), namespace)
        except Exception as exc:
            pytest.fail(f"{doc_path} block {i} failed: {exc}\n\n{block}")
```

**Documentation that doesn't run is documentation that lies.** Executing every snippet in CI means a field rename breaks the build rather than a customer's first experience.

## 20.10 Performance

```
 /docs HTML page                      ~2 KB (the spec loads separately)
 Swagger UI JS + CSS (CDN)            ~1.5 MB, cached by the browser
 Spec fetch, 100 routes               ~300 KB (~30 KB gzipped)
 Swagger UI render, 100 routes        ~1 s
 Swagger UI render, 500 routes        ~5–10 s  ← users assume it's broken
 ReDoc render, 500 routes             ~2 s     ← noticeably better
 Scalar render, 500 routes            ~1.5 s
```

**Optimisations:**

1. **Self-host the UI assets** — removes a CDN dependency and works offline.
2. **Gzip the spec** — ~10× smaller, and it's the dominant transfer.
3. **`defaultModelsExpandDepth: -1`** — the Schemas accordion is the main render cost on large specs.
4. **Prefer ReDoc or Scalar for large APIs**; keep Swagger UI for interaction.
5. **Split very large APIs** into per-audience specs (public vs partner vs internal).
6. **Cache the spec with an ETag** — it changes only on deploy.

## 20.11 Security

```python
# ❌ 1. Public docs on an internal API — a complete attack-surface map (Ch. 19)
# ✔ docs_url=None + openapi_url=None in production, or auth-gate BOTH

# ❌ 2. Gating /docs but not /openapi.json
#    The UI is just a viewer; the spec is the sensitive artifact.

# ❌ 3. Real credentials in examples
description="Example: Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6..."
# ✔ Placeholders only: `Bearer $TOKEN`, `sk_live_xxxxxxxx`

# ❌ 4. A "Try it out" playground hitting PRODUCTION with a shared demo key
# ✔ Point demos at a sandbox with synthetic data; rate-limit demo tokens hard;
#    scope them to demo-only resources

# ❌ 5. CDN-loaded UI assets under a strict CSP, or in an air-gapped deployment
# ✔ Self-host, with subresource integrity if you must use a CDN

# ❌ 6. Documented debug or bypass features
description="Pass ?debug=true to see the full prompt and internal state"
# ✔ If it exists it will be tried in production. Don't ship it.

# ❌ 7. Error examples containing real customer data
# ✔ Synthetic examples, reviewed like code

# ❌ 8. Leaking infrastructure in servers[]
servers=[{"url": "http://internal-api.cluster.local:8080"}]
```

**Docs pages are also an XSS surface.** If you render user-controlled content into a docs template (a tenant name, a custom description), escape it. The docs page runs on your origin with your cookies.

## 20.12 Best Practices

```
✔ Ship Swagger UI (/docs) for interaction and ReDoc or Scalar (/reference) for reading
✔ persistAuthorization: True — stop logging developers out on every reload
✔ defaultModelsExpandDepth: -1 on large APIs
✔ Self-host UI assets; works offline and under a strict CSP
✔ App description = quickstart + auth + limits + errors + versioning
✔ Tag descriptions as section introductions, with links to guides
✔ Generate x-codeSamples from the spec; never hand-write them
✔ A landing page at `/` — an API root should not 404
✔ Errors carry code, actual numbers, retryable, request_id, and doc_url
✔ Deprecation and Sunset headers; a machine-readable changelog endpoint
✔ A playground with a rate-limited demo token for anonymous visitors
✔ Cost and context windows exposed via GET /v1/models
✔ A migration guide from the API you're compatible with
✔ Guides in the repo, next to the code; reference generated
✔ Execute every documentation example in CI
✔ Docs gated or disabled in production for internal APIs
```

## 20.13 Common Mistakes

```python
# ❌ 1. Public docs on an internal API
# ❌ 2. Gating /docs but leaving /openapi.json open
# ❌ 3. No persistAuthorization → re-authenticating on every reload
# ❌ 4. CDN assets in an air-gapped or strict-CSP environment
# ❌ 5. No quickstart → developers leave before their first successful call
# ❌ 6. No examples → developers guess and get 422s
# ❌ 7. Not warning that Try-it-out buffers streams → false bug reports
# ❌ 8. Hand-written code samples → they drift and then mislead
# ❌ 9. Guides in a separate CMS → out of date within a sprint
# ❌ 10. Untested documentation examples → your quickstart 404s
# ❌ 11. Errors without codes or doc links → support tickets instead of self-service
# ❌ 12. No changelog → integrations break with no warning
# ❌ 13. Removing an endpoint with no Deprecation/Sunset period
# ❌ 14. A demo playground pointed at production with a shared key
# ❌ 15. Real tokens or customer data in examples
# ❌ 16. `/` returns 404 → a wasted first impression
```

## 20.14 Interview Questions

1. **What's the difference between Swagger UI and ReDoc?** Swagger UI is interactive with a built-in request executor and auth flow; ReDoc is a read-optimised three-column reference. Both render the same spec; ship both.

2. **Why self-host the UI assets?** The defaults load from a public CDN, which breaks in air-gapped environments, adds a third-party script to your origin, and is blocked by a strict CSP.

3. **What does `persistAuthorization` do?** Keeps the entered token across page reloads. Without it, exploring your API means re-authenticating constantly — the highest-friction default in Swagger UI.

4. **Why hide the Schemas section on large APIs?** `defaultModelsExpandDepth: -1` removes an enormous accordion that dominates both page length and render time when you have dozens of models.

5. **Why does "Try it out" fail behind a proxy?** Swagger sends requests to the selected `servers[]` URL, not the page's origin. A wrong `root_path` or missing server entry sends requests to the wrong host, and cross-origin requests additionally need CORS.

6. **Why does Try-it-out appear to hang on streaming endpoints?** Swagger UI buffers the whole response before rendering. Document this and provide a `curl -N` example instead of letting developers conclude your server is broken.

7. **Where should guides live?** In the same repository as the code, so they're updated in the same pull request and can be executed in CI. Separate CMSs drift within a sprint.

8. **Why generate code samples rather than write them?** Hand-written samples drift the moment a field changes. Generating them from the spec makes drift structurally impossible — the same argument as generating the spec from the code.

9. **What makes an error message good DX?** A stable machine-readable code, the actual numbers involved, whether retrying helps, a request ID for support, and a link to a page explaining the fix.

10. **What are Deprecation and Sunset headers?** RFC 8594 headers signalling that an endpoint is deprecated and when it will be removed, so clients can log warnings and you can measure remaining usage before removal.

11. **Should you expose pricing in the API?** Yes — a `GET /v1/models` with context windows and per-token costs, plus `usage` on every response, lets developers build cost controls. Hiding it makes adoption feel risky.

12. **Why is a playground valuable for an AI API specifically?** The value is in the output, which prose cannot convey. Seeing it work converts far better than reference documentation.

13. **How do you offer a playground safely?** Point it at a sandbox with synthetic data, issue heavily rate-limited demo tokens scoped to demo resources, and never share a production key.

14. **How do you test documentation?** Extract and execute every code block in CI against a live test server. Documentation that doesn't run is documentation that lies.

15. **Why does the API root deserve a page?** It's a common first request. A 404 wastes the first impression; a signpost page routes the visitor to the quickstart, the reference, and the status page.

16. **What belongs in the app-level description?** In order: a working quickstart, authentication, rate limits, the error shape, and the versioning policy — the questions developers ask in their first ten minutes.

17. **How do you sunset an endpoint responsibly?** Mark it deprecated in the spec, add Deprecation and Sunset headers, publish a migration guide, track per-client usage, notify the remaining callers, then remove after the announced date.

18. **What's the highest-converting page for a compatible API?** A migration guide showing the one-line change and honestly listing the behavioural differences.

19. **How do you keep docs fast on a 500-endpoint API?** Self-host assets, gzip the spec, collapse schemas, prefer ReDoc or Scalar for reading, and consider splitting the spec by audience.

20. **What are the security risks of docs pages?** Publishing an internal attack-surface map, real credentials in examples, documented debug bypasses, infrastructure hostnames in `servers[]`, and XSS if user-controlled content is rendered into the page.

21. **Why gate `/openapi.json` and not just `/docs`?** The spec is the sensitive artifact; the UI merely renders it. Gating only the viewer protects nothing.

22. **What's the value of a machine-readable changelog?** Clients can poll it to detect changes affecting them, and it forces you to record what changed — including deprecations with removal dates.

23. **How do docs serve two audiences now?** Humans read the rendered guides and reference; agents consume the same OpenAPI spec as tool definitions. The descriptions you write serve both, which raises the value of writing them well.

24. **What's the right split between generated and written documentation?** Reference is generated (complete and never stale); guides are written (task-oriented and impossible to generate). Attempting either with the wrong tool produces bad docs.

25. **Design the documentation strategy for an AI platform.** Quickstart landing page at `/` with a working curl; Swagger UI at `/docs` with `persistAuthorization` and self-hosted assets; Scalar at `/reference`; generated `x-codeSamples` in curl, Python, and TypeScript; guides in `docs/` in the repo, executed in CI; a sandbox playground with rate-limited demo tokens; errors with codes, numbers, retryability, request IDs, and doc links; `GET /v1/models` exposing cost and capabilities; a changelog endpoint plus Deprecation/Sunset headers; a migration guide from OpenAI; and everything gated behind auth in production for internal services.

## 20.15 Exercises

**Easy**
1. Add a rich app description with a quickstart and confirm it renders as Markdown in both UIs.
2. Enable `persistAuthorization` and `displayRequestDuration`; verify the token survives a reload.
3. Add tag descriptions with links to external guides.

**Medium**
4. Self-host Swagger UI assets and confirm the docs work with the network disabled.
5. Add Scalar at `/reference` and compare render time against Swagger UI on your spec.
6. Implement `add_code_samples` generating curl and Python samples; verify they appear in ReDoc.
7. Add a landing page at `/` linking to docs, spec, guides, and health.

**Hard**
8. Add HTTP Basic protection to both `/docs` and `/openapi.json`, with a test proving the spec is not reachable unauthenticated.
9. Implement documentation-example testing that executes every Python block in `docs/` against a live test server.
10. Build a streaming playground page that renders tokens as they arrive, with an anonymous rate-limited demo token.

**Production**
11. Build the complete docs surface: landing page, Swagger UI, Scalar, generated code samples, guides in-repo with CI execution, changelog endpoint with Deprecation headers, `GET /v1/models` with pricing, a sandbox playground, and a migration guide — with a measured time-to-first-successful-call under five minutes for a new developer.

## 20.16 Solutions

**Solution 9 — executable documentation.**
```python
# tests/docs/test_examples.py
import re, pathlib, pytest

CODE_BLOCK = re.compile(r"```(python|bash)\n(.*?)```", re.DOTALL)
DOC_FILES = sorted(pathlib.Path("docs").rglob("*.md"))

def blocks(path: pathlib.Path):
    for i, (lang, code) in enumerate(CODE_BLOCK.findall(path.read_text())):
        if "# docs-test: skip" in code:
            continue
        yield i, lang, code

@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", DOC_FILES, ids=lambda p: p.name)
def test_doc_examples_run(path, live_server, demo_api_key, tmp_path):
    for index, lang, code in blocks(path):
        code = (code.replace("https://api.example.com", live_server)
                    .replace("$TOKEN", demo_api_key)
                    .replace("sk_live_...", demo_api_key))
        if lang == "python":
            try:
                exec(compile(code, f"{path}:{index}", "exec"), {"__name__": "__doc__"})
            except Exception as exc:
                pytest.fail(f"{path} block {index} failed: {exc!r}\n\n{code}")
        else:                                       # bash
            result = subprocess.run(["bash", "-e", "-c", code],
                                    capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
            if result.returncode != 0:
                pytest.fail(f"{path} block {index} exited {result.returncode}\n"
                            f"{result.stderr}\n\n{code}")
```
**Reasoning:** substituting the live server URL and a real demo key is what makes this a genuine end-to-end check rather than a syntax check. The `# docs-test: skip` escape hatch matters — some blocks are illustrative fragments (a `diff` snippet, a partial config) that can't run, and without an escape hatch teams disable the whole test at the first false failure. `bash -e` ensures a failing curl in a multi-line block actually fails the test.

**Solution 10 — the streaming playground.**
```python
@app.get("/playground", include_in_schema=False, response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def playground(redis: RedisDep) -> HTMLResponse:
    demo_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
    # Heavily limited: 5 requests, 15 minutes, sandbox data only.
    await redis.setex(f"demo:{demo_token}", 900,
                      json.dumps({"requests_remaining": 5, "scope": "demo"}))
    return templates.TemplateResponse("playground.html",
                                      {"demo_token": demo_token})
```
```html
<!-- templates/playground.html — the streaming client, in ~25 lines -->
<textarea id="prompt">Summarise the attached quarterly report.</textarea>
<button id="send">Send</button>
<pre id="output"></pre>
<script>
document.getElementById('send').onclick = async () => {
  const output = document.getElementById('output');
  output.textContent = '';
  const response = await fetch('/v1/chat/completions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json',
              'Authorization': 'Bearer {{ demo_token }}'},
    body: JSON.stringify({
      messages: [{role: 'user', content: document.getElementById('prompt').value}],
      stream: true}),
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    const err = await response.json();
    output.textContent = `Error: ${err.error.message}`;
    return;
  }
  const reader = response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
  let buffer = '';
  while (true) {
    const {done, value} = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    buffer += value;
    const parts = buffer.split('\n\n');
    buffer = parts.pop();
    for (const part of parts) {
      const line = part.split('\n').find(l => l.startsWith('data: '));
      if (!line) continue;
      const data = line.slice(6);
      if (data === '[DONE]') return;
      const event = JSON.parse(data);
      if (event.type === 'delta') output.textContent += event.content;
      if (event.type === 'error') output.textContent += `\n[${event.code}] ${event.message}`;
    }
  }
};
</script>
```
**Reasoning:** this doubles as the reference client implementation. Developers open devtools, read 25 lines, and understand your streaming protocol completely — including the in-band error handling from Chapter 9 that a status-code-only client would miss. A playground that also teaches the protocol is worth several pages of prose.

## 20.17 Mini Project — A Complete Developer Portal

**Goal.** Take a developer from landing page to first successful API call in under five minutes.

**Requirements:**
1. Landing page at `/` with a working curl, links, and status.
2. Swagger UI at `/docs`: self-hosted assets, `persistAuthorization`, collapsed schemas, custom branding.
3. Scalar at `/reference` for reading.
4. Generated `x-codeSamples` for curl, Python, and TypeScript on every operation.
5. App description with quickstart, auth table, rate-limit table, error shape, and versioning policy.
6. Tag descriptions linking to guides.
7. `docs/` in-repo with guides for streaming, RAG, webhooks, error handling, and migration from OpenAI — every example executed in CI.
8. Streaming playground with anonymous rate-limited demo tokens against sandbox data.
9. `GET /v1/models` with pricing, context windows, and capabilities.
10. `GET /v1/changelog` plus Deprecation and Sunset headers on deprecated routes.
11. Errors with `code`, actual numbers, `retryable`, `request_id`, and `doc_url`.
12. Production gating: docs and spec behind auth or disabled.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A developer who has never seen the API makes a successful call in under five minutes (measure this with a real person).
- Docs work with the network disabled (self-hosted assets).
- Every documentation example passes in CI.
- The playground streams tokens visibly and handles in-band errors.
- Every error response includes a working `doc_url`.
- The generated TypeScript SDK's method names read naturally.
- `/openapi.json` returns 401 for anonymous users in production.

## Chapter 20 Summary

| Idea | The one-line version |
|---|---|
| Swagger UI to try, ReDoc/Scalar to read | ship both; they cost three routes |
| `persistAuthorization` | the single highest-value UI setting |
| Self-host the assets | offline, CSP-safe, no third-party script on your origin |
| The description is your quickstart | it's the first thing anyone reads |
| Generate code samples | hand-written ones drift and then mislead |
| Warn about streaming in Try-it-out | it buffers, and developers assume you're broken |
| Errors are documentation | code + numbers + retryable + request_id + doc_url |
| Guides in the repo, reference generated | each with the right tool |
| Execute documentation in CI | docs that don't run are docs that lie |
| A playground converts AI products | the value is in the output, not the prose |
| Gate the spec, not just the UI | the spec is the sensitive artifact |

### Cheat Sheet

```python
FastAPI(swagger_ui_parameters={
    "persistAuthorization": True, "displayRequestDuration": True,
    "defaultModelsExpandDepth": -1, "filter": True, "docExpansion": "list",
    "tryItOutEnabled": True, "operationsSorter": "alpha"})

get_swagger_ui_html(openapi_url=..., title=...,
                    swagger_js_url="/static/swagger-ui-bundle.js",
                    swagger_css_url="/static/swagger-ui.css")
get_redoc_html(openapi_url=..., title=...)

operation["x-codeSamples"] = [{"lang": "cURL", "source": "..."}]
schema["info"]["x-logo"] = {"url": "..."}

# Deprecation (RFC 8594)
Deprecation: true
Sunset: Wed, 31 Dec 2025 23:59:59 GMT
Link: <https://docs.example.com/migrate>; rel="deprecation"
```

### Production Checklist
- [ ] Landing page at `/`; `/docs` and `/reference` both available
- [ ] Self-hosted UI assets; works offline
- [ ] `persistAuthorization` enabled; schemas collapsed on large APIs
- [ ] Quickstart, auth, limits, errors, and versioning in the description
- [ ] Generated code samples in three languages
- [ ] Guides in-repo, executed in CI
- [ ] Changelog endpoint; Deprecation/Sunset on deprecated routes
- [ ] `GET /v1/models` exposing cost and capabilities
- [ ] Time-to-first-successful-call measured with a real developer

### Security Checklist
- [ ] Both `/docs` and `/openapi.json` gated or disabled in production
- [ ] No real credentials, customer data, or internal hostnames in examples
- [ ] No documented debug or bypass features
- [ ] Playground points at a sandbox with hard-limited demo tokens
- [ ] User-controlled content escaped in docs templates
- [ ] Subresource integrity if any CDN asset remains

### Performance Checklist
- [ ] Spec gzipped and ETagged
- [ ] Schemas accordion collapsed
- [ ] ReDoc/Scalar preferred for large specs
- [ ] Very large APIs split by audience
- [ ] Docs render time measured, not assumed
